subject: english-literature
title: Lines and Stanzas
welcome_lead: Before sense, a poem is shapes on a page. Learn the parts.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on lines, stanzas and basic poetry layout.
final_note: You can now name a poem's basic visual building blocks.

concepts.def: One row of words in a poem.

walkthroughs.body_html: A line is one row of poetry; a stanza is a group of lines separated by a blank line — like a paragraph in prose.
A couplet = 2 lines, often rhyming. A quatrain = 4 lines, very common in pop songs and ballads.
Enjambment is when sense flows over a line break without a pause. It creates speed or surprise.

mcqs.q: Line that runs on without a pause is.
Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.

mcqs.q: Why distinguish the speaker of a poem from the poet?
options: The speaker is whoever reads the poem out loud.
The speaker of a poem is always the poet themselves.
The speaker is the voice constructed in the poem; the poet is the writer. Treating them as identical can mislead, especially with dramatic monologues or personae.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
